summary: A full IELTS paper with strong distractors in every part: an airport taxi booking, a sports-centre reopening talk, a student-tutor discussion and a lecture on chocolate. All keys are correct; one accepted answer broke the word limit and was removed.
strengths: Part 1: the twelfth corrected to the twenty-second, six o'clock moved to half past five, MAPEL corrected to MAPLE, the standard car price given but not used, card discouraged for cash.
Part 2 MCQs give two wrong reasons each before the right one (flooding repaired long ago, pool heating next year), and the box separates "temporarily closed" (tennis) from "will open later" (sauna).
Part 3 is a natural tutor discussion where each option is weighed and dismissed with a reason.
Part 4 notes paraphrase well for most items ("to suit their taste" for "far too bitter for European mouths", "most cacao" for "seventy per cent of the world's beans").

issues.problem: "half past five" was accepted for a gap marked ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER (three words).
issues.change: Accepted answers are now "5.30", "5:30" and "five thirty" in mock6-listening.js.

issues.problem: Some Part 4 notes echo the lecture exactly (Q31 "whipped the paste into a bitter {{31}}", Q32 "flavoured with chilli and {{32}}", Q37 "first solid chocolate {{37}}").
issues.change: Reword, e.g. Q32 "spiced with chilli and {{32}}", Q37 "1847: first chocolate {{37}} you could eat".

issues.problem: Q28 option "the choice of vegetarian dishes" is said word for word by Madina when she sums up.
issues.change: Reword, e.g. "the range of meat-free food".
